who: Wojciech 'Wojtek' Gula (akadmin / Supreme Leader) - the operator this project is built for
why: Room furniture and decor should carry his own touches, so the office reads as HIS, not as a generic asset pack. Per ADR-061, operator taste wins on look.

props: a worn electric bass on a stand
a bass amp with a cable coiled on top
a wall hook holding a strap
a small rack with blinking LEDs
a patch panel with labelled cables
a packing-crate stack with stencil-ish marks and NO readable words
traits.note: No Polish or any language text baked into art - readable third-party text is what we are removing elsewhere.

traits.fact: loves Japanese cars; owns a 30-year-old Mazda MPV; likes old Honda Civics
props: a boxy 1990s Japanese minivan seen from the side as a wall poster, plain, no badges
a small die-cast car on a shelf
traits.note: NO manufacturer badges or logos. A recognisable-but-unbranded boxy van is fine; a Mazda/Honda mark is not.

props: an orange tabby asleep in a box
a black-and-white cat on a chair
traits.note: Generate OUR OWN cats. The shipped cats spritesheet is LimeZu non-commercial art (ADR-060) and must not ship.

props: an unbranded manga shelf with plain spines
an orange-and-blue arcade cabinet with no logo or text
a small CRT with a colourful abstract game paused on it
traits.note: The ENERGY only. Dragon Ball and Pokemon are third-party trademarks: no characters, no ball/creature silhouettes, no logos, no title text. This is the same rule that is removing the FRIENDS sign and the film posters.

rule: Every personal prop goes through the normal pipeline: generated in the room's declared 30-degree isometric projection, keyed, gated by check_prop_alignment, placed on a declared grid cell or wall anchor, with a manifest. Personal inclinations do not exempt a prop from the gate or the licence rule.
how_to_use: add the wanted props to profiles/rooms/<agent>_room.json with a grid cell, then run scripts/gen_room_set.py
